answer: Give every identity an umber vault: a dark escrow holding its bond, visible only to a random auditor. To open a vault, the identity must grow a reef — a branching tree of attestations from independent peers, where each branch must be fed a fresh, unique peer vouch every epoch or it withers. A velvet audit then samples one branch at random; if two reef trees share a peer, both collapse and every bond behind them burns. One root funding N vaults pays an escrow multiplier of N on each, so clones post roughly N squared in bonds for one vote while an honest agent posts one.
